description: The merge phase rebases in the OPERATOR'S checkout, so one uncommitted line anywhere in the repo fails the merge — and because a refused rebase is classified REBASE-CONFLICT, it is then re-dispatched to the agent for the full RETRY_MAX. Observed twice in one afternoon in cuneiform: 011 and 012 each completed all their stories, each failed to merge over a single modified tracked file (`docs/roadmap/README.md`, 1 insertion), and each burned 3/3 attempts before being left failed — six wasted agent iterations for work that was already done, plus two blocked dependents. 78 makes the failure DIAGNOSABLE; this makes it not happen, and makes it cheap when it does. The operator was editing their own repo while a run was in flight, which is a reasonable way to work: `chief run` checks the tree ONCE at startup and nothing re-checks it at merge time, so the gate cannot actually protect the merge it exists to protect.

userStories.title: A refused rebase is never re-dispatched to the agent
userStories.description: Re-running an agent cannot clean an operator's working tree, so retrying a refusal spends a full iteration to fail identically. Make the retry decision read 78's new classification.
acceptanceCriteria: `retryable_status` (engine/driver.sh:1660) returns FALSE for the refusal state 78 introduces, while REBASE-CONFLICT with ≥1 conflicted path stays retryable exactly as today — the retry exists because a real conflict decays as base moves, and a refusal has no such property

A refused tasklist is left failed after ONE attempt, and the run summary's reason names the precondition (the dirty/locked checkout) plus the operator fix, rather than 'exhausted its retries (3/3)' which reads as a hard problem
The dependents of a refused tasklist are still BLOCKED with the same message shape as today (this story changes what is retried, not the dependency semantics)
A hermetic test asserts the attempt count: a branch whose rebase is REFUSED runs its agent exactly ONCE, and a branch with a real content conflict still retries up to RETRY_MAX
Bash 3.2 compatible; `bash -n` + `shellcheck -S error` clean; `VERSION` bumped (test/version-bump.sh)
userStories.notes: retryable_status() denies REBASE-REFUSED explicitly (above the catch-all); the run summary gains a refusal block naming the cause, 'one attempt, deliberately', the operator's move and the .rebase-refused.md note. test/rebase-refusal.sh extended (agent-turn counter + a dependent tasklist). OBSERVED: bash test/rebase-refusal.sh rc=0 PASS — refused branch attempts=1, agent turns=1, no '↻ retrying', no 'exhausted its retries'; real conflict attempts=3/3 with the retry announced; rr-refuse-dep state=blocked with 'needs "rr-refuse", which FAILED in this run'. Also green: retry-on-failure rc=0, smoke rc=0, noworkguard rc=0, version-bump rc=0 (VERSION 0.8.49), doc-sync rc=0 (README v0.8.49), quality ratchet rc=0 (no metric regressed). bash -n clean; shellcheck 0.11.0 -S error clean on engine/driver.sh + test/rebase-refusal.sh (the two SC1072 hits in bin/chief and engine/quality.sh reproduce on main untouched — pre-existing, that shellcheck version misparses a backtick in a comment).

userStories.title: The merge phase stops requiring a clean operator checkout
userStories.description: Decide and implement how the merge phase integrates without depending on the state of the operator's working tree.
acceptanceCriteria: The merge phase (engine/driver.sh:~1500, the `git checkout "$branch"` + `git rebase "$work_base"` pair inside the merge lock) no longer fails because the operator's checkout has uncommitted TRACKED changes to files the merge does not touch

The approach is chosen explicitly between (a) `git rebase --autostash`, (b) an explicit stash/restore around the critical section, and (c) performing the rebase+verify+merge in a dedicated worktree so the operator's checkout is never checked out onto the branch at all — with the decision and the rejected alternatives recorded in the story notes. (c) is the structural fix and (a) is one flag; whichever is chosen must state why

OPERATOR DATA IS NEVER LOST: if the chosen approach stashes, the restore runs on EVERY exit path including the failure and abort arms (the existing `trap … EXIT` + `$STATE/$name.critical` marker is the precedent), and a restore that cannot replay cleanly leaves the stash INTACT and names it in the run output rather than dropping it. A test kills the driver mid-critical-section and asserts the operator's uncommitted change is still recoverable
A genuine content conflict still behaves exactly as it does today — this story removes a precondition, it does not change conflict handling

A hermetic test asserts the field case end to end: an operator checkout with a modified tracked file the branch does not touch, a branch strictly ahead of main, merge succeeds and the operator's modification survives the run unchanged
Bash 3.2 compatible; `bash -n` + `shellcheck -S error` clean; `VERSION` bumped
userStories.notes: DECISION: (b) an explicit stash/restore around the WHOLE critical section — merge_stash_push/merge_stash_pop in engine/driver.sh, armed from the existing `trap … EXIT` + $STATE/<name>.critical marker, and applied to the merge queue's identical critical section too. REJECTED (a) `git rebase --autostash`: it pops the moment the rebase ends, so the operator's edit is back in the tree for the merge-time re-verify and the --no-ff merge — the gate would be measuring the branch PLUS someone's half-finished work, and it covers only 1 of the 3 git commands here (the checkout before it and the merge after it stay exposed). test/dirty-checkout.sh pins this: the fixture's verify hook FAILS if it can see the operator's marker. REJECTED (c) rebase+verify+merge in a dedicated worktree, on two counts. run_verify runs the project's hook with cwd = the work repo, and real gates lean on untracked, unclonable state there (node_modules, target/, .env, a warm build cache) — a fresh worktree per merge either fails the gate or pays a cold build every merge. And the merge has to land ON the base branch, which the operator's checkout holds; a linked worktree cannot check out that same branch, so it would merge detached and move refs/heads/<base> by hand, leaving the operator's working tree silently BEHIND its own HEAD — a quiet corruption traded for a loud, recoverable refusal. DATA SAFETY: three restore paths — the subshell EXIT trap (happy path + every failure/abort arm), teardown's .critical sweep (signal), the next run's preflight sweep (SIGKILL, where neither ran); the work lives only in git's own stash, applied BY SHA (never stash@{0}) with --index so staged state comes back staged; a replay that cannot apply DROPS NOTHING and the run summary names `git -C <repo> stash apply <sha>`. Conflict handling is untouched. OBSERVED: test/dirty-checkout.sh rc=0 PASS (new; registered in .chief/verify.sh's CHIEF_BYSTANDER_TESTS, test/all.sh's BASH_SUITE and .github/workflows/ci.yml) — the field case merged @c854a6a with docs.txt+staged.txt restored byte-identical and staged.txt still staged, `git stash list` empty, `verify: ok` at merge time, and a SIGKILL mid-critical-section left the entry intact for the next run to hand back. Also green: rebase-refusal rc=0 (its refusal scenario moved from uncommitted dirt — no longer a refusal — to a stray .git/rebase-merge; a stray MERGE_HEAD does NOT work, `git checkout` clears merge state), conflict-forensics rc=0, retry-on-failure rc=0, merge-batch rc=0, teardown rc=0, smoke rc=0, noworkguard rc=0, version-bump rc=0 (VERSION 0.8.50), doc-sync rc=0 (README v0.8.50), quality-ratchet rc=0, chief lint: 5 tasklist(s) clean, check-doc-links 6 dead refs / 4 targets (unchanged — pre-existing plan-review.md pairs). bash -n clean; shellcheck 0.11.0 -S error clean on engine/driver.sh, engine/mergequeue.sh, test/dirty-checkout.sh, test/rebase-refusal.sh.

userStories.title: The startup cleanliness gate says what it actually protects
userStories.description: Reconcile the startup check with the merge-time reality now that the merge no longer depends on a clean tree.
acceptanceCriteria: The startup gate's refusal message and `FORCE=1` escape hatch are re-stated for what they now protect — the AGENT's view of the repo at launch — rather than implying they protect the merge, which they never did (they are checked once, and nothing re-checks at merge time)

If US-2 lands (c) (merge in a dedicated worktree), evaluate whether the startup gate should still block at all or merely warn, and record the decision — a gate that stops a run for a condition the run no longer depends on is friction without protection

`FORCE=1` remains able to start a run on a dirty tree, and the docs (README/docs) say plainly that editing the repo DURING a run is safe for the merge phase once this lands, since that is the workflow that produced the field failures
No behaviour change is asserted for a clean tree — a run that starts clean behaves byte-identically
userStories.notes: DECISION on criterion 2: US-2 landed (b) stash/restore, NOT (c) a dedicated worktree, so the conditional does not fire — and the gate STAYS A BLOCK, not a warning. What changed is the ground it stands on. It never protected the merge (checked ONCE at startup, nothing re-checks; the field failures walked straight past it) and since US-2 there is nothing left there to protect — the merge phase parks the work repo's uncommitted work for its critical section. What it does buy is the AGENT's FORK POINT: every worktree is created from the base branch TIP (wt_git add … "$work_base"), never from the working tree, so uncommitted work is invisible to every tasklist in the run and the agent builds against a base the operator has already moved past — unrepairable after the fact, unlike the merge-time exposure. Downgrading to a warning was considered and rejected on exactly that asymmetry. CHANGED: the two refusal messages (the dirty-tree one now names the fork point, says editing DURING a run is fine for the merge, and says when FORCE=1 is the right call; the off-base one names why base matters — it also stopped hardcoding 'main' in the dirty message and uses $BASE_BRANCH), a 24-line header comment above the gate, the FORCE=0 line in driver.sh's env header, README (new 'Working in the repo while a run is in flight' section + Contents entry), and docs/explanation/drivers-and-safety.md (two new bullets: the operator's checkout is not part of the floor; the startup gate protects the agent — plus the now-stale 'uncommitted tracked changes' refusal cause marked as no longer reachable). OBSERVED: test/dirty-checkout.sh rc=0 PASS with a new section D — on a dirty tree `chief run` exits non-zero, the refusal names the condition + 'AGENT forks from' + 'DURING a run is fine' + FORCE=1, and creates NO branch, NO worktree and NO status file; FORCE=1 on that same dirty tree merges (status MERGED) with the operator's marker still in docs.txt and `git stash list` empty. Clean-tree behaviour is untouched — nothing in the changed block runs when the gate passes: smoke rc=0, noworkguard rc=0, rebase-refusal rc=0, quality-ratchet rc=0, version-bump rc=0 (VERSION 0.8.51), doc-sync rc=0 (README v0.8.51), chief lint 5 tasklist(s) clean, check-doc-links 6 dead refs / 4 targets (unchanged baseline). bash -n clean; shellcheck 0.11.0 -S error clean on engine/driver.sh and test/dirty-checkout.sh.

userStories.title: `chief run` must not silently override an env-set DRY_RUN
userStories.description: An independent invocation footgun found in the same session: DRY_RUN=1 in the environment is discarded, so a command intended as a simulation performs a real run.
acceptanceCriteria: `bin/chief run` sets `local dry=0` and then passes `DRY_RUN="$dry"` to the driver, which OVERRIDES an inherited `DRY_RUN=1` with `0` — so `DRY_RUN=1 chief run` silently performs a REAL run. Fix it so an env-set `DRY_RUN` is honoured (the `--dry-run`/`-n` flag still wins when passed), matching the driver's own `DRY_RUN="${DRY_RUN:-0}"` convention at engine/driver.sh:205

Audit the other toggles forwarded the same way in that block (PARALLEL, CHIEF_PROVIDER, CHIEF_MODEL, AUTO_MERGE_MAIN, CHIEF_VERBOSE) and apply the same rule — a flag overrides the environment, an unset flag does not clobber it — or record why a given one should differ

A test asserts `DRY_RUN=1 chief run` spawns no agent, creates no worktree and no branch: this was observed in the field launching a real tasklist that was then only caught by the appearance of a worktree
Bash 3.2 compatible; `bash -n` + `shellcheck -S error` clean; `VERSION` bumped

userStories.title: A branch that bumps a SUBMODULE gitlink can merge
userStories.description:
The sharpest instance of US-2, and it does not need an operator to leave anything uncommitted — chief creates the dirt itself and then refuses over it.

`wt_busy()` (engine/driver.sh:793) tests `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no`. Git does not update a submodule working tree on checkout, so the instant a branch whose gitlink differs from the current one is checked out, git reports ` M <submodule>`. If that branch's PURPOSE is to advance the pin, the change it exists to make is the thing that blocks it — on every run, forever.

Measured 2026-08-17 in ~/Development/chief-cloud, tasklist 76-runner-0-8-alignment (the pin bump 31a3e4d v0.7.25 -> c9edac7 0.8.40, i.e. chief's own submodule in chief-cloud):

| step | `git status --porcelain` |
|---|---|
| on main | 0 entries |
| `git checkout chief/76-runner-0-8-alignment` | 1 entry — ` M chief` |
| `git submodule update --init` | 0 entries |

It refused three consecutive runs and read REBASE-REFUSED each time, while `git status` looked clean to the operator between attempts, because chief restores main on the way out. 77-submodule-currency-guard — the tasklist for keeping submodules current — was blocked behind it, so the cycle was closed. 76 was ultimately hand-merged (chief-cloud edd2af2).

NOTE: if US-2 moves the rebase into a worktree, this may be fixed incidentally — submodules are not initialized in linked worktrees (`git submodule status` there reads `-<sha>`). Incidental is not enough; assert it.
acceptanceCriteria: A branch whose only change is a submodule gitlink bump rebases and merges without operator intervention.

`git submodule update --init --recursive` runs after the branch is checked out and BEFORE cleanliness is tested, so the tree honestly matches the ref rather than the check being loosened. `--ignore-submodules=dirty` is the wrong fix and must not be used: it hides changes INSIDE a submodule's working tree, not the gitlink mismatch this is, so it would not even work here.
A submodule with genuine uncommitted changes inside it STILL blocks the merge. Assert this explicitly, or the fix trades a loud failure for a silent one.

A behavioural test in `test/` stands up a repo with a submodule, bumps the gitlink on a branch, and drives a full run through to merge. Without it this regresses the next time the checkout order moves.

The REBASE-REFUSED report distinguishes ' M <submodule>' from ordinary uncommitted work and names `git submodule update` as the fix — the current text says 'commit or stash them', and neither commits nor stashes a gitlink mismatch.
